primitives.name: Temporal Stimulus Patterning
primitives.verbatim_quote: THE PATTERNING OF STIMULUS COMPOUNDS 379 MAJOR COROLLARY V Differential reinforcement applied to temporal stimulus compounds results in the patterning of such compounds, either positively or negatively according to whether the compound or the components are reinforced.
primitives.assumptions: Differential reinforcement is applied to temporal stimulus compounds; patterning occurs based on whether the whole compound or individual components are reinforced.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When reinforcement is not differentially applied to components versus compound, no discernible patterning emerges.

layer2.mapping: Behavioral patterning corresponds to information-theoretic entropy reduction in stimulus-response mappings within GSE state-space.
layer2.telemetry: Observed deviation from baseline response patterns under varying reinforcement schedules.

primitives.verbatim_quote: A distinctly unsuccessful attempt at a formula for this latter type of reaction tried out in an earlier study (4) was, where R1 is the amplitude of the reaction evoked by one stimulus component, and R, is the amplitude of that evoked by a second.
primitives.assumptions: Reaction amplitude varies continuously with stimulus magnitude; empirical formulas require physiological limits.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Formula fails when reaction type is non-all-or-none (e.g., galvanic skin response).

layer2.mapping: Amplitude data serves as kernel input for GSI probabilistic modeling of reaction likelihoods.
layer2.telemetry: Measured reaction amplitudes across multiple stimulus components.

These insights form a dual framework: one rooted in probabilistic inference (GSI) and another in topological state transitions (GSE). Failure modes include lack of reinforcement differentiation and absence of clear primary principles in configuration theory.
